name: Quiet weekend at Hartle Barn
summary: A first silent weekend for forty people, secular, with a teacher leading sits and giving instruction. Forty-five-minute sits and two hours of silent walking a day. £95.
description:
Four times a year we take the barn for a weekend and forty people spend it in silence. It is designed for people who have not done this before, and most of each weekend is first-timers.

Sam leads it. Sam has taught meditation in a secular setting for fifteen years and does not use the vocabulary of any tradition. There are anchor sessions: an opening on Friday evening where everything is explained, a guided sit at nine and at four each day, a walk at two, and a closing on Sunday afternoon where people speak for the first time. Between the anchors the time is yours: sit in the barn, sit in the field, or go back to your B&B and sleep.

The sits are forty-five minutes, on cushions or chairs as you prefer, and Sam talks you through them. The walk at two is two hours, in silence, in single file, up onto the ridge behind the barn and along it and down. It is not a stroll; it climbs three hundred feet and the ground is rough in places. We think the walking is what makes the sitting work for people who have never sat, and we ask that everyone come on it.

The whole weekend is silent from Friday evening to Sunday afternoon, including in the barn kitchen and on the ridge. You will be given a card to show people in the village.

It is a moderately physical weekend. The sits are long for a first time and the walks are real. If you want a weekend that asks nothing of your body this is not it.
practical: Friday 7pm to Sunday 4pm, four weekends a year. £95 including lunch on Saturday and Sunday; you arrange your own accommodation in the village, and we send a list. Chairs and cushions provided. Bring a blanket, a flask, boots, and a waterproof. Honiton station is seven miles; there is a bus on Saturdays only. The barn has two steps at the door.
